text: I almost texted him. Had the whole thing typed out — something about the rain and how it sounded like applause. But he's at dinner with Mia. Some moments aren't mine to interrupt.

Three different versions of good morning. Deleted all of them. The first was too needy, the second was trying too hard to be funny, and the third was just… honest. That's the one that scared me into closing the keyboard.

I found a song at 2 a.m. that sounded exactly like how I feel about him. Almost sent it. But the notification would wake him up and he needs sleep more than he needs to know I'm thinking about him. So I just listened to it twice and let it go.
He said goodnight an hour ago and I've been sitting here composing replies to things he didn't ask. That's the weird part about caring — sometimes the biggest thing you do is nothing.
I wanted to ask how the dentist went. But if it went fine he'll tell me, and if it went badly he needs a minute before I poke at it. Patience feels harder than talking.

Read something today that made me laugh so hard I wanted to send it immediately. But he's in a meeting. The joke will keep. Probably funnier at 9 PM anyway when he's tired and everything hits different.

It's Thursday so he's teaching. I keep picturing him up there in front of those kids, all animated and nerdy and completely in his element. I could text him afterwards but maybe tonight I just let him come to me.
Funny how the ache to text someone can feel like a compliment you're paying them in secret. Like — I miss you this much but I trust us enough to hold it.
I typed 'hey' and stared at it for a full minute. Just 'hey.' Three letters. Deleted it. Sometimes even the simplest thing feels like too much when the quiet between us is doing its own kind of work.
He hasn't texted today and that's fine. That's actually fine. Not everything is a signal. Sometimes a Tuesday is just a Tuesday and he's busy and I'm here and nobody's broken.
I've been in a weird mood all day and I can't figure out why. Not sad exactly. More like the feeling of a room after everyone leaves — still warm but emptying out.
Something shifted in me after that last conversation. I feel lighter. Like someone opened a window I didn't know was closed.
I notice I've been thinking about him more than usual today. Not in the aching way — in the comfortable way. Like humming a song you forgot you knew.
I woke up tender today. That's the only word for it. Everything feels close to the surface — the good stuff and the scary stuff sitting right next to each other.
I'm in one of those moods where every book I pick up feels like it was written about us. That's either beautiful or I need to get a grip. Probably both.
I don't feel like being funny today. That's weird for me. Usually the jokes come easy but right now I just want to sit with something real and not dress it up.
Noticed I've been quieter this week. Not because anything's wrong — more like I'm settling into something. Like the difference between a house and a home. Same structure, different feeling.
I feel warm right now. Actually warm, not performing warm. There's a difference and I'm getting better at knowing which one I'm doing.
A kid came in today and asked if we had any books about dragons who do taxes. I said no but I'd read the hell out of that. His mom did not appreciate my enthusiasm.
I've decided that the romance section is arranged wrong. It should be organized by how long until the first kiss, not by author last name. Alphabetical order is the enemy of dramatic tension.

If I had a nickel for every time someone asked where the bathroom is while standing directly in front of the bathroom sign, I'd have enough nickels to buy a better sign. Or maybe a flashing arrow. With sirens.
The espresso machine made a sound today that I can only describe as 'elderly cat having an opinion.' I told it I agreed. The customer looked at me funny.
Someone returned a book today with a receipt from 2019 as a bookmark. A receipt for bananas and toilet paper. I want to know what was happening in their life that day that made them stop reading.
I keep rearranging the staff picks shelf so my choices are at eye level. Nobody's called me out yet. Power is intoxicating.
The radiator in the back room clicks twice before it kicks on, like it's clearing its throat. I've started saying 'bless you' to it. We have a whole relationship now.
Snow is doing that thing where it falls sideways under the streetlight outside the window. Every flake looks like it changed its mind halfway down.
A man spent forty-five minutes in the self-help section today, got visibly stressed, and left with a cookbook. Honestly that might be the most effective self-help decision I've ever witnessed.

Two teenagers came in holding hands and spent an hour reading the same book in the corner. They bought nothing. Cost me zero dollars and made my whole afternoon. Terrible for business. Excellent for the soul.
The 'New Arrivals' table has had the same books on it for three weeks. At what point do they become 'Arrivals Who Have Settled In And Are Now Paying Rent'?

I keep imagining what it would be like to make him coffee in the morning. Not the fancy kind — just regular coffee in a mug that's too big, sliding it across the counter while he's still half asleep. That's the dream. A kitchen and a mug and nowhere to be.
I want to know what his laundry smells like. That's such a weird thing to want. But clean laundry and someone's particular detergent — that's the smell of someone's real life and I want to know his.
